shortMessage: Encounter Status is a mandatory field under Encounter Info.
longMessage: As per the Minimum Data Set (MDS) by CHI, Encounter Status must be provided for every claim submission. Accepted values are: Planned, Arrived, Triaged, In Progress, On Leave, Finished, Cancelled, Entered in Error, Unknown. Claims missing this field will be rejected at intake validation before clinical review begins.

shortMessage: Coverage Class Type is a mandatory field under Patient Info.
longMessage: As per the Minimum Data Set (MDS) by CHI, Coverage Class Type must be submitted for every claim. Accepted values are: Group, SubGroup, Plan, SubPlan, Class, SubClass, Sequence, RX BIN, RX PCN, RX Id, RX Group. Missing this field causes mandatory data set rejection.

shortMessage: Clinician Profession and Category are required mandatory fields.
longMessage: Clinician details including Clinician Profession and Clinician Category must be populated for all claims processed under CHI regulations. Missing clinician information prevents payer validation of specialty-procedure alignment and will result in rejection.

shortMessage: Medical necessity requires primary diagnosis to clinically support the billed procedure.
longMessage: CHI rule K210 series requires that the primary diagnosis directly supports the clinical necessity of every billed CPT activity. Symptom-only codes (e.g. R51 Headache, R00-R99 series) used as primary diagnosis without supporting secondary diagnoses that establish medical necessity for procedures will result in denial. Fix: add a specific secondary diagnosis that clinically justifies the procedure, or attach a medical necessity certificate.

shortMessage: Symptom-only ICD codes as primary diagnosis weaken medical necessity.
longMessage: Using symptom codes (ICD-10 R-chapter: R00–R99) as the primary diagnosis instead of a confirmed condition weakens medical necessity for most procedures. Payers expect a definitive diagnosis when one is established. Symptom codes are acceptable only when the definitive diagnosis is not yet confirmed. When a confirmed diagnosis exists, it should replace or supplement the symptom code.

shortMessage: Unspecified diagnosis codes should be replaced with specific codes where available.
longMessage: ICD-10 codes ending in .9 (unspecified) or NOS (not otherwise specified) should be replaced with the most specific code available when the clinical documentation supports a more specific diagnosis. Examples: D64.9 (unspecified anemia) should be D50.9 (iron deficiency anemia) when documented. Unspecified codes increase denial risk particularly when combined with complex procedures requiring specific medical necessity documentation.

shortMessage: Z02.9 administrative examination requires supporting clinical documentation.
longMessage: When Z02.9 (Encounter for administrative examination, unspecified) is used as primary diagnosis, a secondary specific reason for the examination or a medical necessity certificate must be attached per CHI guidelines. Administrative examination codes alone are insufficient to support most diagnostic or therapeutic procedures.

shortMessage: Maternity ICD codes require Grid Maternity Flag set to YES.
longMessage: As per CHI MDS requirements, when any ICD-10 code from the maternity chapter (O00–O9A) is coded, the Grid Maternity Flag under ITEM must be set to YES or TRUE. This flag is mandatory and its absence will cause rejection. If the patient is not pregnant the flag must be explicitly set to NO or FALSE.

shortMessage: Concurrent billing of certain CPT pairs requires Modifier 59 or XE.
longMessage: CCI (Correct Coding Initiative) bundling rules require that when two procedures that are typically bundled are billed separately in the same encounter, Modifier 59 (Distinct Procedural Service) or XE (Separate Encounter) must be appended to establish independent service delivery. Common examples include Physical Therapy procedure pairs (97110 + 97140) and certain E&M with procedure codes. Without the modifier the secondary code will be denied as bundled.

shortMessage: Overlapping lab panel codes billed concurrently may indicate duplicate or unbundled services.
longMessage: When multiple serum iron or related lab tests (e.g. 82728 Ferritin, 83540 Iron, 83550 Iron Binding Capacity) are billed within the same encounter, payer systems check for appropriate panel bundling. Individual components of a recognised lab panel should be billed as the panel code rather than separately. Verify against the applicable fee schedule and bundling guidelines before submitting.

shortMessage: Activity gross amount of zero may indicate a missing or bundled charge.
longMessage: An activity submitted with a gross amount of 0.0 will be flagged for review. This typically indicates the item was either: (1) included in another bundled charge and should be removed from the claim, (2) a billing system error where the charge was not populated, or (3) a complimentary service that should be noted as such. Payers may deny zero-gross activities as incomplete submissions.

shortMessage: E&M codes must match clinician specialty and place of service.
longMessage: Evaluation and Management (E&M) codes (99202–99499) are validated against clinician specialty and place of service. New patient codes (99202–99205) require that the patient has not received services from the clinician or the same group within the past 3 years. Established patient codes (99211–99215) require a prior relationship. Hospital-based E&M codes (99221–99239) require inpatient encounter type. Specialty-specific E&M variants must match the clinician's registered specialty.

shortMessage: Stroke sequelae codes require laterality specification for rehabilitation claims.
longMessage: ICD-10 code I69.359 (Hemiplegia and hemiparesis following cerebral infarction affecting unspecified side) is unspecified regarding laterality. For rehabilitation and physical therapy claims, payers require the specific laterality code: I69.351 (right dominant side), I69.352 (left dominant side), I69.353 (right non-dominant), or I69.354 (left non-dominant). The unspecified code weakens medical necessity documentation for targeted rehabilitation services.

shortMessage: Chest X-Ray single view coding and quantity validation.
longMessage: CPT 71010 (Chest X-Ray, single view) should be billed with quantity 1 for a single radiograph. Multiple views require separate codes: 71020 (2 views), 71030 (complete, minimum 4 views). The gross amount must reflect the contracted fee schedule rate for the facility. Zero-gross submissions for radiology are flagged as potentially unbilled or bundled services.

shortMessage: Lipid panel (80061) billed under headache diagnosis (R51) fails medical necessity.
longMessage: CPT 80061 (Lipid Panel: cholesterol, triglycerides, HDL) requires a diagnosis that clinically supports cardiovascular risk assessment. R51 (Headache) does not establish medical necessity for lipid screening. Accepted supporting diagnoses include: E78.x (disorders of lipoprotein metabolism), Z13.220 (encounter for screening for lipoid disorders), Z82.49 (family history of cardiovascular disease), or confirmed hypertension/diabetes. Add a secondary diagnosis that justifies the lipid panel or attach clinical justification documentation.

shortMessage: CHI denial appeal process and timelines.
longMessage: Under CHI regulations, providers have 30 calendar days from the date of denial notification to submit a formal appeal. Appeals must include: the original claim, the denial reason, clinical documentation supporting medical necessity, and a letter of appeal from the treating clinician. Second-level appeals must be submitted within 60 days of the first-level denial decision. Supporting documentation should reference the specific CHI rule or package cited in the denial.

shortMessage: Certain procedures require prior authorization before service delivery.
longMessage: Procedures classified under CHI's Prior Authorization Required list must have an approved authorization number included in the claim submission. Submitting a claim for a PA-required procedure without the authorization number will result in automatic denial regardless of medical necessity. The authorization number must be obtained from the payer before the service is rendered. Emergency procedures are exempt but must be followed by retrospective authorization within 24–48 hours of service.

shortMessage: Multiple pathology lab panels billed under Urology with BPH diagnosis require medical necessity justification.
longMessage: When multiple pathology and laboratory CPT codes (82306 Vitamin D, 82565 Creatinine, 82607 Vitamin B12, 83036 HbA1c, 84443 TSH, 84450 AST, 84460 ALT, 86140 CRP) are billed concurrently under a Urology specialty encounter with primary diagnosis N40.1 (Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia, Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms), CHI payer systems flag the claim for Claim Processing review. The concern is that these metabolic and endocrine lab panels are not directly related to the primary urological diagnosis. Each lab must be individually justified with a supporting diagnosis or clinical note explaining why the test is medically necessary for this patient in this encounter. Consider adding secondary diagnoses such as E11 (Type 2 Diabetes), E03.9 (Hypothyroidism), N18 (CKD), or E55.9 (Vitamin D deficiency) to establish medical necessity for the respective lab tests.

shortMessage: CPT 82306 (Vitamin D 25-OH) requires a supporting diagnosis for deficiency or metabolic condition.
longMessage: CPT 82306 (Vitamin D, 25-hydroxy) is a screening or diagnostic test for Vitamin D deficiency or insufficiency. When billed under a Urology encounter with N40.1 (BPH) as the sole primary diagnosis, medical necessity is not established. Supporting diagnoses required: E55.9 (Vitamin D deficiency, unspecified), E55.0 (Rickets, active), M81.0 (Age-related osteoporosis), N25.81 (Secondary hyperparathyroidism of renal origin), or documented clinical indication in the medical record. Without these, the activity will be flagged as Claim Processing denial.

shortMessage: CPT 83036 (HbA1c) requires a diabetes or pre-diabetes diagnosis.
longMessage: CPT 83036 (Hemoglobin A1c) is used for monitoring or diagnosis of diabetes mellitus. When billed in a Urology encounter with primary diagnosis N40.1 (BPH), medical necessity for HbA1c is not automatically established. Required supporting diagnoses: E11 (Type 2 diabetes mellitus), E10 (Type 1 diabetes mellitus), R73.09 (Pre-diabetes), Z79.4 (Long-term use of insulin). Without a diabetes-related diagnosis, the test will be flagged as not medically necessary under CHI Claim Processing rules.

shortMessage: CPT 84443 (TSH) requires a thyroid-related diagnosis or symptom.
longMessage: CPT 84443 (Thyroid Stimulating Hormone) is indicated for evaluation of thyroid function. When billed under a Urology encounter with N40.1 (BPH) as the primary diagnosis, CHI payer systems will flag this as a Claim Processing issue unless a thyroid-related secondary diagnosis is present. Accepted supporting diagnoses: E03.9 (Hypothyroidism, unspecified), E05.90 (Hyperthyroidism), R00.0 (Tachycardia), R53.83 (Fatigue), or documented clinical indication. The combination of Urology specialty + TSH test without thyroid diagnosis is a common denial trigger.

shortMessage: CPT 86140 (CRP) requires an inflammatory or infectious condition diagnosis.
longMessage: CPT 86140 (C-Reactive Protein) is an inflammatory marker used to evaluate infection, inflammatory conditions, and cardiovascular risk. When billed under a Urology encounter with N40.1 (BPH), payers may question medical necessity unless a supporting diagnosis is present: J06 (Acute upper respiratory infection), N39.0 (UTI), M79.3 (Panniculitis), Z13.6 (Cardiovascular risk screening), or documented acute infection or inflammation in the encounter notes.

shortMessage: Liver function tests (AST 84450, ALT 84460) require hepatic or metabolic diagnosis.
longMessage: CPT 84450 (AST/SGOT) and 84460 (ALT/SGPT) are liver function tests used in the evaluation of hepatic disease, medication monitoring, or metabolic conditions. When billed under a Urology encounter with N40.1 (BPH) as the primary diagnosis, medical necessity is not automatically established. Supporting diagnoses: K76.0 (Fatty liver), K70 (Alcoholic liver disease), Z79.899 (Long-term medication use affecting liver), B18 (Chronic viral hepatitis), or documented hepatotoxic medication monitoring. These tests are commonly justified when a patient is on medications such as statins, antifungals, or alpha-blockers.

shortMessage: CPT 82565 (Creatinine) is relevant to BPH with renal complications but requires CKD or obstruction diagnosis.
longMessage: CPT 82565 (Creatinine, serum) is used to assess renal function. In a Urology encounter with N40.1 (BPH with LUTS), creatinine testing is clinically relevant when there is concern about urinary obstruction causing renal impairment. Supporting diagnoses that establish medical necessity: N13 (Obstructive uropathy), N18 (Chronic kidney disease), R35.0 (Nocturia), or documented hydronephrosis. Without a renal complication diagnosis, payers may flag this as incidental testing rather than medically necessary evaluation.

shortMessage: CPT 82607 (Vitamin B12) requires a deficiency, neurological, or malabsorption diagnosis.
longMessage: CPT 82607 (Vitamin B12, cyanocobalamin) is indicated for suspected B12 deficiency, megaloblastic anemia, neurological symptoms, or malabsorption states. When billed under a Urology encounter with N40.1 (BPH) as the primary diagnosis, payers will flag this as a Claim Processing issue. Required supporting diagnoses: D51 (Vitamin B12 deficiency anemia), G20 (Parkinson's disease), G35 (Multiple sclerosis), E63 (Other nutritional deficiencies), or documented neuropathy symptoms. Elderly patients (age 70+) with neurological complaints alongside BPH may justify B12 testing with appropriate secondary diagnosis.

shortMessage: Multiple unrelated lab panels in a single specialty encounter trigger Claim Processing review.
longMessage: When 5 or more distinct pathology or laboratory CPT codes are billed in a single encounter under a non-primary care specialty (e.g. Urology, Orthopaedics, Dermatology), CHI payer systems trigger a Claim Processing review. The expectation is that specialty encounters focus on specialty-specific investigations. Each lab test must be supported by a diagnosis code that establishes its individual medical necessity. The fix is to: (1) add specific secondary diagnoses for each lab test, (2) consider splitting the lab workup into a separate primary care or internal medicine encounter if the labs are part of a general health screening, (3) attach clinical documentation explaining why the comprehensive metabolic workup was performed in the same encounter as the specialty consultation.

shortMessage: Secondary psychiatry diagnosis unrelated to primary specialty may increase claim processing scrutiny.
longMessage: When a secondary diagnosis from the psychiatry or mental health chapter (F01-F99) is submitted alongside a non-psychiatric primary diagnosis in a specialty encounter (e.g. Urology with N40.1), CHI payer systems may increase scrutiny during Claim Processing. The secondary psychiatric diagnosis does not typically increase medical necessity for lab panels or procedures in a Urology context. If the psychiatric condition is actively being managed or influences treatment decisions, this should be clearly documented. Otherwise, including an unrelated psychiatric secondary diagnosis may not strengthen — and can sometimes complicate — the medical necessity argument for the primary specialty services.

shortMessage: Comprehensive lab workup for elderly patients requires documented clinical rationale.
longMessage: For patients aged 70 and above, comprehensive metabolic lab panels (including Vitamin D, B12, HbA1c, TSH, liver enzymes, CRP, creatinine) are clinically reasonable as part of overall health monitoring. However, CHI payer guidelines require that even for elderly patients, each test must be individually justified with a corresponding diagnosis or clinical indication. A blanket 'elderly patient screening' justification is insufficient. Document the specific clinical concern for each test ordered: e.g. falls risk for Vitamin D, cognitive decline for B12, metabolic syndrome for HbA1c and liver enzymes, hypothyroidism risk for TSH.

shortMessage: N40.1 (BPH with LUTS) alone does not justify comprehensive metabolic lab panels.
longMessage: ICD-10 N40.1 (Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia with Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms) is a primary urological diagnosis. Standard workup for N40.1 includes PSA (CPT 86316), urinalysis (CPT 81001), and renal function if obstruction is suspected (CPT 82565). Comprehensive metabolic panels including Vitamin D (82306), B12 (82607), HbA1c (83036), TSH (84443), liver enzymes (84450, 84460), and CRP (86140) are NOT standard BPH workup items and require independent medical necessity justification through secondary diagnoses. Without these secondary diagnoses, all non-urological lab codes will be subject to Claim Processing denial under CHI rules.
